extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for scholarly journals / research publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for individuals asked to peer review manuscripts for scholarly journals, covering conduct before, during, and after review, plus conflicts, confidentiality, and handling ethical concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely response to review invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is courteous to respond to an invitation to peer review within a reasonable time frame, even if you cannot undertake the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to the invitation whether accepting or declining; a timely decline allows editors to seek alternative reviewers and speeds the editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare expertise and scope limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should declare if they do not have the subject expertise required to carry out the review or if they are able to assess only part of the manuscript, outlining clearly the areas for which they have the relevant expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contacted, indicate areas you can competently assess and be explicit if parts of the manuscript are outside your expertise so the editor can make an informed decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest alternative reviewers appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: If you cannot review, it is helpful to make suggestions for alternative reviewers if relevant, based on their expertise and without any influence of personal considerations or any intention of the manuscript receiving a specific outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend alternatives strictly on the basis of expertise; avoid suggesting collaborators, close colleagues, or anyone where a personal consideration might bias the process or the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an unbiased, constructive critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should provide an unbiased, constructive critique of the manuscript that is objective and helpful to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on constructive feedback that helps authors improve the work; avoid letting personal preferences or relationships affect the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rewrite the manuscript; suggest clarity improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not attempt to rewrite the manuscript to your own preferred style if it is basically sound and clear; suggestions for changes that improve clarity are, however, important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer phrasing or structural suggestions only to clarify meaning or strengthen presentation, not to impose stylistic preferences. Recognize the paper belongs to the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair, honest and unbiased assessment of strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Bear in mind that the editor requires a fair, honest, and unbiased assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both positive and negative aspects; provide balanced comments that help editors make informed decisions rather than one-sided critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and support criticisms with evidence/references
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific in your criticisms, and provide evidence with appropriate references to substantiate general statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague assertions; cite relevant literature or provide concrete examples from the manuscript to justify critiques and suggested corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal, derogatory or aggressive comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Review reports should be balanced and considerate; never personal. Avoid making statements that may be perceived as personal critiques or aggressive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critique around the work, not the authors. Removing ad hominem language and inflammatory tone increases usefulness and professionalism of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality and do not misuse manuscript content
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat any manuscripts received as confidential documents. Do not retain or copy the manuscript. Do not share the manuscript with any colleagues without the explicit permission of the editor. Do not contact the authors directly without the permission of the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use information obtained during the peer review process for your own or another's advantage; after the review you must still maintain confidentiality and not exploit privileged information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and manage conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should declare all potential conflicts of interest, seeking advice from the journal if they are unsure whether something constitutes a relevant interest. Do not allow conflicts of interest to influence acceptance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose financial, personal, professional, or competitive conflicts promptly; if a conflict is significant, decline the review and advise the editor so they can choose an impartial reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected ethics violations to the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: If you come across any irregularities with respect to research and publication ethics, let the journal know. Do not attempt to investigate on your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report concerns such as suspected misconduct in research/writing, substantial similarity to other submissions or published articles, or other ethical issues to the editor; provide relevant evidence but do not conduct independent probes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly and consistently to revision review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond promptly to requests to review revised manuscripts. Try to maintain a consistent approach across versions. Be available to provide additional advice if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asked to re-review, compare revisions against your earlier comments, apply the same standards, and be prepared to clarify prior recommendations if editors request further input.
